name: {N} {X} explained
description: Classic listicle / explainer — a numbered bundle of short, independent topics around a unifying theme. Each chapter is a self-contained question or claim with hook → explanation → micro-payoff. Pairs natively with the Listicle / Explainer format and the BrainWise compilation video layout.
subjectLabel: Theme (e.g. paradoxes, sleep mysteries, plane crashes)
openingDevice: Open with a punchy framing of the unifying theme — one or two sentences that promise the listener N independent payoffs in the next ~30 minutes. Tease the most counter-intuitive item in the list ('one of these has been baffling physicists for 80 years…') without revealing the answer. End the cold-open with a clean handoff: 'Here are {N} {X}, explained.'
bodyStructure: Chapter 1: Strongest hook — the topic that earns the YouTube click. Open with a question or counter-intuitive claim, explain in 2-4 supporting beats, close with a memorable micro-payoff

Chapters 2-{lastButOne}: Each chapter is one independent topic. Same shape every time: hook → explanation → micro-payoff. Vary tone slightly (some surprising, some evidence-rich, some wry) so the listicle doesn't feel monotone. NO narrative threads carry between chapters — they are standalone
Chapter {last}: Save a satisfying / punchy topic for last so the video ends strong, not fizzles. Could be the most surprising, the most resonant, or the one that recontextualizes the whole list
closingDevice: Close with a one-paragraph zoom-out: what these {N} items together suggest about the theme. Avoid 'and so we've learned…' textbook closers — let the factual surprise carry it. Optional: tease the next listicle in the series.
